title: Healthy-aging propulsion decline, certified: the vertical-GRF push-off peak falls ~0.012 BW per decade (OLS slope bit-for-bit vs scipy.stats.linregress and base R lm)

dataset.name: GaitRec -- large-scale ground reaction force dataset of healthy and impaired gait
dataset.record: healthy controls (n=208, ages 15-78); age + vertical-GRF push-off peak (grfLandmarks 3rd landmark); shod, standardised speed, baseline sessions
dataset.citation: Horsak B, Slijepcevic D, Raberger AM, Schwab C, Worisch M, Zeppelzauer M. GaitRec, a large-scale ground reaction force dataset of healthy and impaired gait. Scientific Data 2020;7:143. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0481-z.

proposition: The push-off peak (late-stance propulsion, driven chiefly by the ankle plantarflexors) declines with age. In GaitRec healthy controls (n=208, ages 15-78), each subject's push-off peak comes from the certified grfLandmarks; the NEWLY-AUTHORED linearRegression regresses it on age, reproducing scipy.stats.linregress BIT-FOR-BIT and base R stats::lm to machine precision. The slope is -0.00120 BW/year (-0.012 BW/decade; intercept 1.144 BW), t(206)=-4.61, p~7.0e-6, R-squared 0.094 -- a modest but highly significant healthy-aging propulsion decline.

claims.statement: OLS slope of push-off peak on age (BW per year; negative = decline)
push-off decline per decade of age (BW)
OLS intercept (modelled push-off at age 0, extrapolated)
R-squared: fraction of push-off variance explained by age
-log10(two-sided slope p): the age effect is highly significant
|linearRegression slope - base R lm slope| (machine precision, < 1e-9)
the slope is negative (push-off peak declines with age)

validation.reference: The newly-authored linearRegression op (simple univariate OLS) is validated against BOTH scipy.stats.linregress AND base R stats::lm/summary.lm on the identical (age, push-off) pairs -- a double reference. scipy.stats.linregress agrees BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0 for the slope and R-squared; both use the closed-form estimator) and base R lm agrees to machine precision (|diff| ~ 1e-18 on the slope; lm uses a QR path). The per-subject push-off peaks come from PhysioMoCap::grfLandmarks (3rd landmark; certified in the sibling gait-grf-gaitrec case).
validation.data: REAL -- GaitRec (Horsak et al. 2020), vertical-GRF push-off peak vs age, healthy controls (n=208, ages 15-78)
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) linearRegression reproduces scipy.stats.linregress bit-for-bit and base R lm to machine precision; (2) the push-off peak declines with age in healthy controls. HONEST scope: (1) this AUTHORS A NEW OP, linearRegression (simple univariate OLS), and reuses the certified grfLandmarks op (validated in the sibling gait-grf-gaitrec case) for the push-off peak (its 3rd landmark); (2) the OLS slope, R-squared and slope p-value reproduce scipy.stats.linregress BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0; both use the closed-form estimator) and base R stats::lm to MACHINE PRECISION (|diff| ~ 1e-18 on the slope; lm uses a QR path); (3) the finding: in healthy controls (n=208, ages 15-78) the push-off peak DECLINES with age at a slope of -0.00120 BW/year (-0.012 BW/decade; intercept 1.144 BW), t(206) = -4.61, p ~ 7.0e-6, R-squared 0.094 -- a modest but highly significant healthy-aging propulsion decline (age explains about 9% of the between-subject variance in push-off); (4) the regression SLOPE gives the RATE of decline, which a correlation alone does not; (5) HONEST LIMITS: the GaitRec healthy-control age distribution is young-skewed (median 32, only 2 subjects over 70), so the slope is best interpreted over the well-sampled 15-55 range; this is a CROSS-SECTIONAL association (age differences between people, NOT within-person change over time) and NOT causation; one processed vGRF per subject; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The healthy-control age distribution is young-skewed (only 2 subjects over 70), so the linear slope may understate the decline at older ages where ankle push-off power is known to drop more steeply; a cohort with denser older sampling (or a non-linear/spline fit) would refine the trajectory. This is also cross-sectional, not longitudinal. The single linear slope is the most interpretable first-order rate. Documented, not escalated.
